findings.title: No reader path to install and invoke the CLI
findings.problem: The README provides only contributor setup and tests. It does not tell a prospective user how to install the package, run its `pebble-count` command on a file, or what result to expect.
evidence: `pyproject.toml` declares a distributable project named `pebble-count` and a `pebble-count = "pebble_count:main"` console-script entry point (lines 5-15).
The implementation accepts one required file path and prints the count (src/pebble_count/__init__.py lines 12-16).
The current commit removed a prior README “Getting started” section containing installation, invocation, and expected-output guidance.
findings.impact: Readers can understand the utility's definition but cannot reach its primary CLI capability without inspecting packaging metadata and source code; the visible commands instead imply that development setup is the only supported path.
findings.correction: Restore a short user-oriented install-and-run example before Development, including the required file argument and that the command prints the non-blank-line count.

commands.command: pwd && rg --files -g 'README*' -g '!node_modules' -g '!vendor' && git status --short && git log -1 --oneline

nl -ba README.md && rg --files -g '!node_modules' -g '!vendor' -g '!*.lock' | sort && find . -maxdepth 2 -type f -not -path './.git/*' | sort && git show --stat --oneline HEAD && git show --format=fuller --no-ext-diff HEAD -- README.md
nl -ba pyproject.toml && nl -ba src/pebble_count/__init__.py && nl -ba tests/test_pebble_count.py && git ls-files -s LICENSE COPYING NOTICE 2>/dev/null || true && git log --oneline --all -- README.md

verification: Reviewed the README, package metadata, CLI implementation, test fixture, repository file inventory, and the current README change history.
limitations: The package was not installed or executed; this finding is supported by the declared console entry point and its implementation.
